svg.title: MarkeTech frontend: the path of a request
svg.desc: Panel A: in development, npm run dev (or npm run dev:link on Windows, through a link) starts Vite, which serves the source files and passes /api and /_allauth to the Django backend, and /ws as a WebSocket. In production the image is built by GitHub Actions on a push to develop or main that changes the code, and published from main only: the Dockerfile runs vue-tsc and vite build, which write dist, and Nginx serves it, answering index.html for every application address and passing /api, /_allauth, /admin, /static and /ws/ to the backend container; a reverse proxy outside the repository ends HTTPS in production. The nginx.conf directives are detailed in infra-compose-stack.svg, panel C. Panel B: the browser, outside the repository, loads index.html, then main.ts loads Poppins 400 and 600, creates the Vue application with the i18n and router plugins and mounts App.vue, which lays out the header, the side bar, the RouterView and the footer; the router has 27 routes, and RouterView displays the page matching the address, such as HomePage.vue for /; the 24 pages and the frame components are listed in frontend-architecture.svg, panel A. Panel C: the frame and the pages call session.ts or the nine domain files of src/api/, which go through src/api/http.ts, the only file that calls fetch; the requests reach Django on the same origin through the Vite proxy or Nginx, and urls.py is detailed in backend-request-flow.svg, panel C. In real time, live.ts opens one WebSocket to /ws/ per tab while someone is logged in; the server side is detailed in realtime-signal-flow.svg, panel A; the server sends signals, and the listeners registered with onNews read again through the API. Panel D: moving between pages with RouterLink or router.replace uses pushState or replaceState and does not ask the server for a new page.
svg.text: MarkeTech frontend: the path of a request
From the address typed by the user to the page on screen, from the page to the backend, and back in real time. Follow the numbers 1 to 17.
Real files of the repository: frontend/ package.json, vite.config.ts, Dockerfile, nginx.conf, index.html, src/ (main.ts, router.ts, i18n,
App.vue, components, pages, session.ts, api/, live.ts). General view: frontend-architecture.svg.
Two servers for the same files
Vite on the workstation · Nginx in Docker, on your PC or in production
in the browser, each time an address is opened or refreshed
in the browser, when a page sends a form, needs data, or hears news
no new page is asked from the server

svg.text: production only; absent on your PC
Almost the same rule on both servers, so the code in the browser (panels B and C) never knows which one answers
A file that exists is sent as is. Any other address gets index.html: the application chooses the page.
/api, /_allauth and /ws go to the backend on both servers, /ws as a WebSocket. Nginx alone also passes /admin and /static.

svg.text: The server only says what changed: { type: "messages" | "applications" | "appointments", application: 12 }.
The listener reads again through src/api/ (steps 12 to 14 again), so the API alone decides what the user
may see. After a cut, and when the tab comes back to the front, every listener hears null: read all again.
